mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in WORKPLACES from the prior weeks signals reduced commuter density, which directly suppresses impulse retail visits within one to two weeks and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent level over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10 and TRANSIT falls below -10 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline further within 14 days after simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT weakness, or instead rises above its last-4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while PARKS collapses, households shift discretionary time indoors and defer outing-based spending, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken over the next four weeks as outside recreation substitutes disappear.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its previous 4-week average over the following 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying high and PARKS staying low.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT indicates mobility suppression from policy or risk aversion, and retail visits lag this shock by about one week because shopping trips are cut after commuting channels contract.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next weekly observation after a TRANSIT drop larger than 15 points, or rises above the recent baseline instead.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains very high while WORKPLACES is weak, routine errand traffic substitutes for discretionary retail visits and the next four weeks show below-baseline retail recreation activity.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 35 while WORKPLACES stays below 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite sustained high grocery/pharmacy trips and weak workplace mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from a deep negative trough marks improved outdoor leisure conditions, which spills into more discretionary outing activity and lifts RETAIL_REC after a short two-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from the prior week after being below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after a PARKS rebound from below -20, or continues to fall relative to the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals people are staying home and compressing trip chains; that behavioral contraction reduces retail footfall for the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower than its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: The mechanism activates only under renewed containment conditions: when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop sharply, discretionary retail is cut immediately and stays below the recent average for two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 2 weeks after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop more than 15 points in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL combined with stagnant or falling RETAIL_REC implies substitution toward home-based activity, which becomes self-reinforcing and keeps retail recreation below baseline over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds to above its last-4-week mean within 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated.
